title: Parallel identical submissions create duplicate complaints
module: Complaints (also visitors, service requests, SOS, deliveries, mess feedback)
steps: Log in as a student; send the same complaint 5 times in parallel (simulated double-click / flaky network).
expected: One complaint stored; the other requests get 409 Conflict.
actual: All 5 requests returned 201 and 5 identical complaints were stored (check-then-insert race).
resolution: Added a per-user PostgreSQL advisory lock (services.lock_for_user) around duplicate checks in every create endpoint. Retest NFT-21: 1 x 201 + 4 x 409, 1 record stored.

title: Visitors page scrolls sideways on a 375 px phone screen
steps: Log in as a student on a 375 x 812 viewport and open Visitors.
expected: No horizontal scrolling; tables scroll inside their card.
actual: Page width 503 px > 375 px viewport; whole page scrolled horizontally.
resolution: Cards inside CSS grids now use min-width: 0 so wide tables scroll within the card. Retest NFT-18: no overflow on 8 pages x 3 widths.

title: Database connections exhausted at 300 concurrent users
steps: Run k6 with 300 virtual users against the API started with 2 workers.
actual: 0.82 % failed requests, p99 32 s. Log: 'remaining connection slots are reserved' and 'QueuePool limit ... timed out' – 2 workers x 50 pooled connections exceeded PostgreSQL max_connections (100).
resolution: Pool made configurable (DB_POOL_SIZE / DB_MAX_OVERFLOW / DB_POOL_TIMEOUT) with defaults sized to the 40-thread request pool (35 + 5 per worker). An intermediate setting (10 + 5) caused 7 % pool time-outs and was rejected. Retest at 300 users: 0 % errors, average 1.4 s.

title: Personal data is not encrypted at rest (NFR06)
steps: Inspect the users and visitor_requests tables in PostgreSQL.
expected: Personal data (phone, registration number, visitor details) encrypted in storage.
actual: Passwords and OTPs are bcrypt-hashed, but phone numbers, registration numbers and visitor phone numbers are plain text.
resolution: Planned: column-level encryption (pgcrypto or application-side Fernet) for PII, plus a managed database with encryption at rest and TLS (sslmode=require).

title: Response time grows about 21x from 50 to 300 concurrent users
steps: Run k6 at 50, 150 and 300 users on the same 2-vCPU machine that also runs PostgreSQL and the load generator.
expected: No significant degradation (p95 at 300 users <= 2 x p95 at 50 users).
actual: p95 92 ms at 50 users vs 1,921 ms at 300 users; throughput levels off at about 162 requests/s (CPU-bound). Still within the 3 s average target.
resolution: Re-test on production-sized hosting; scale horizontally (more workers/instances), cache dashboard counts, move the load generator off the server.

title: Firefox and WebKit (Safari) could not be tested in this environment
expected: Smoke test runs in Firefox and WebKit.
actual: browserType.launch: Executable doesn't exist – the sandbox network policy blocks the Playwright browser downloads.
resolution: On a normal machine run 'npx playwright install firefox webkit' then 'npm run test:all-browsers' in e2e/.

title: Test-script defects found while running the suites
found_by: First runs: NFT-23 (pytest); FT-06, FT-08, FT-30, NFT-10, NFT-16, NFT-17 (Playwright)
steps: (a) NFT-23 checked audit entries created by tests that run later; (b) E2E locators such as getByLabel('Category') also matched filter/search inputs; (c) a CSS selector used a React id containing ':'; (d) a Tab key press happened before the page rendered; (e) run_all_tests.sh stored the PID of a wrapper shell instead of the load-test server, so the server kept running and later exhausted PostgreSQL connections (HTTP 500 in the NFT runner).
expected: Tests independent of order and with unambiguous selectors.
actual: 7 false failures in the first runs (1 pytest, 6 Playwright), 3 more while fixing selectors, and one aborted pipeline run (e) – none were application defects.
resolution: NFT-23 now performs its own actions; E2E tests use name-based selectors and wait for rendering; the pipeline starts the server with 'exec' and waits for the port to close. All affected tests were re-run with the complete pipeline.

title: Status filter drop-down stretched across card headers
module: UI components (Visitors, Services, SOS, Gate desk)
found_by: Manual visual review of screenshots (not detected by automated tests)
steps: Log in as a warden and open Visitors.
expected: Card title on the left, compact filter on the right.
actual: The filter used the full-width input style, so it filled the header and wrapped the card title onto two lines.
resolution: FilterSelect now has its own auto-width style. Frontend unit tests and the full Playwright suite were re-run afterwards.

title: Login fails with HTTP 500 when running on the built-in SQLite database
found_by: User report – local run on Windows with SQLite (not covered: automated suites used PostgreSQL)
steps: Start the app without DATABASE_URL (SQLite file), log in once, then log in again.
actual: TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes in auth.login – SQLite returns dates without a time zone.
resolution: All date/time columns now use a UTCDateTime type that always returns time-zone-aware UTC values. Re-tested: backend suite 60/61 and browser suite 23/23 on SQLite (the remaining SQLite case is the PostgreSQL-only parallel-submit lock, NFT-21); 61/61 and 23/23 on PostgreSQL.
